name: Boston cream pie
origin: Despite the name, a cake, not a pie — from Boston, Massachusetts, first served at the Parker House Hotel in the 1850s; a sponge cake split and filled with pastry cream, glazed with chocolate on top. Declared the official dessert of Massachusetts in 1996.

process.name: cream butter and sugar
process.description: beat butter and sugar until light

process.name: fold in flour
process.description: fold in flour, leavening and salt

process.name: bake
process.description: bake in a round pan, then split horizontally once cooled

notes: A standard American butter-sponge hybrid, between a genoise and a Victoria sponge in richness, chosen for a crumb sturdy enough to be split and filled. The pastry cream filling and chocolate glaze that make this a 'Boston cream pie' rather than a plain sponge are separately-prepared components applied after baking, out of scope for this batter's formulation.
